- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of low sentiment (0.00–0.33) follow a high price, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid prolonged underestimation.  
- Model consistently overpredicts in early forecast horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, forecast should revert toward that average within 7–10 days.  
- Avoid forecasting >10% above prior 30-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) and confirmed over 3+ days.
